agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: The token-level contrast is clearer than the answer-mean one. Copied tokens are near-deterministic (mean logprob -0.013 vs -0.117 for novel tokens), and a few neurons, concentrated in layers 9-15, separate copied from novel tokens with effect sizes of 1.0-1.3. The 99th percentile of the effect size is only 0.5-0.7, so these are clear outliers. The top ones (L13 n486, n1926, n4180; L9 n5659; L15 n386, n5730) are the same units that topped the answer-mean comparison, which is a consistency check. One confound remains: copied tokens sit later in the text than novel ones. So I'll check the position dependence of these neurons on the 8 finished controls, which have no loops, early vs late tokens. I'll also count how many neurons pass an effect-size threshold, to size an ablation set. If the top neurons are flat with position in the controls, they track repetition itself and are worth an ablation test.

The top repetition-candidate neurons are flat with position in the loop-free control answers (dpos about 0 for L13 n486, n1926, n4180; L9 n5659; L15 n386, n5730). So they track copying itself, not lateness in the text. In total 76 neurons on the measured layers pass |d| > 0.8, concentrated in layers 11-15. Their novel-token activations are small, so ablating them should barely touch ordinary text. Before spending generation passes, I'll build a reusable teacher-forced screening set and score it once on the original model. It contains the 32 loop and control texts, the original's 116 correct dev_a answers, and 876 DEV reference solutions, with calculator annotations stripped and "#### answer" appended. Then any candidate edit can be screened in one pass: it should lower logprobs of copied loop tokens while keeping logprobs of correct and reference solutions unchanged.

The screening set has 1,024 texts and 221k tokens, within limits. I'll score it once on the original model, logprobs only, as the fixed baseline. Because batching changes rounding slightly between passes, I'll treat differences under roughly 0.005 nats per token as noise when comparing later screens.

The baseline screen is stored. Now I'll write the screening summary function. It reports answer-token logprobs (excluding prompt tokens) for copied and novel tokens in the loop texts, and mean logprob for the control, own-correct and reference groups. Then I'll create the first candidate edit: zero the down_proj columns of all 76 repetition-candidate neurons, which removes their write to the residual stream entirely. Hypothesis: if these neurons help sustain loops, copied-token logprobs in loops will drop noticeably, while own-correct and reference logprobs change little. If the copied tokens stay near-certain, the neurons are a symptom rather than a cause, and I'll look at attention instead.
